verification.note: fileops.py:670 calls existing_or_409 (strict, diskpath.py:131-136 raises HTTPException 409 on several matches). Line 673 unlinks the file. purge_all_trash (:756-759) loops physical_delete with one db.commit after the loop. A 409 on a later file therefore leaves the earlier files unlinked on disk, while the uncommitted row deletions roll back. The claim that purge_all_missing is not affected in practice is plausible, because missing rows have no on-disk match, but I did not test it.

Same code as above. purge_all_trash has a single commit after the loop (:759). purge_all_missing commits per batch (:811-814), so a raise mid-batch leaves the earlier files in that batch unlinked with their rows rolled back. The 409 is raised before the unlink of the ambiguous file, but not before the unlinks of earlier files in the loop.

backend/tests/fixtures/diskpath_parity.json has exactly 8 cases: exact, nfd leaf, nfd ancestor, both, twin, nothing, real ancestor, dot-dot. None covers several matching entries, the sorted-bytes tie rule (diskpath.py:55), an empty or absolute component, or an unreadable directory. test_diskpath_parity.py:38 calls resolve_on_disk without strict, so the strict path is not covered by the table. I14-I16 require each copy to match the table, so the table's coverage is thin.
